reasoning: The only model that completed its review (qwen3-235b) found all files safe. The package follows standard AUR patterns: PKGBUILD uses a known safe split-package idiom with eval/declare-f for function generation, sources point to official upstream GitHub repos with proper checksums, and all metadata files are standard. The other two reports were inconclusive due to tool errors (LLM response parsing failures and content safety filter triggers), not security findings.
disagreement_analysis: Disagreement caused by infrastructure failures, not security findings. deepseek-v4-flash failed to parse its PKGBUILD verdict despite producing reasoning. openrouter/free's content safety filter triggered on .nvchecker.toml (a benign TOML config), producing an unparseable 'User Safety: unsafe' response with irrelevant categories. Neither represents actual security concerns.
coverage_issues: deepseek-v4-flash: PKGBUILD review failed with LLMResponseError despite producing valid reasoning in logs
openrouter/free: .nvchecker.toml review failed due to content safety filter triggering on benign configuration file
false_positives: openrouter/free 'unsafe' verdict on .nvchecker.toml: content safety filter triggered on standard version-checking config, not a real security finding
learnings: Content safety filters can trigger on benign files (TOML configs, documentation) and produce unparseable responses - need to detect and handle these as tool errors rather than security findings
LLM response parsing can fail even when models produce valid security reasoning - need fallback extraction or retry logic
Distinguish between 'model produced reasoning but verdict parsing failed' (tool error) vs 'model found no issues' (safe verdict)
Advisory reports with content safety triggers should be flagged as tool failures, not counted toward disagreement
